data_description.channels: Create a target / entity for each channel
data_description.nodes: Note that selecting all nodes can create tens or hundreds of entities in Home Assistant depending on the Meshtastic network size

web_client.description: Experimental: serves the Meshtastic web client so you can work with the gateway by hand through Home Assistant's connection to it, since the radio takes one client at a time. Home Assistant admins open it from the Meshtastic sidebar, which issues a token for the gateway; the web client has full admin control of the gateway.

tcp_proxy.description: Experimental: You can enable meshtastic tcp proxy if you like to interact with your gateway manually as well. Note that meshtastic devices only allow one single connection, so this integration will pose as a meshtastic device and the tcp client will connect to home assistant rather directly to the device. Connecting directly to the meshtastic device will interrupt the home assistant connection. Using python cli, use 'meshtastic --host homeassistant:port'

chat.title: Mesh Chat
chat.description: Adds a "Mesh Chat" panel to the sidebar to read and send channel and direct messages through this gateway. Messages are kept in Home Assistant, including the ones sent from the chat. Unlike the web client and TCP proxy, the chat uses Home Assistant's own login and does not open a second connection to the node.

data.require_admin: Only administrators can use the chat
data.prefix_sender: Prefix messages with the sender's name

data_description.require_admin: Turn off to let every Home Assistant user read and send messages through this gateway.
data_description.prefix_sender: Messages sent from Home Assistant all come from the gateway node. Turn on to add the Home Assistant user's name, e.g. "Alex B.: on my way", so others on the mesh know who wrote it.
data_description.history_size: Older messages are removed once a channel or direct message conversation reaches this size.
data_description.channel_management: Lets users create, rename, re-key, enable or disable channels on this gateway from the channel details in the chat. Every change is confirmed first. Off: channels are read-only in the chat.

tcp_proxy.name: Meshtastic TCP Proxy
tcp_proxy.description: Experimental: You can enable meshtastic tcp proxy if you like to interact with your gateway manually as well.  IMPORTANT SECURITY CONSIDERATION: Meshtastic protocol is unauthenticated, enabling this option gives everybody control over your gateway that can reach your Home Assistant installation. Note that meshtastic devices only allow one single connection, so this integration will pose as a meshtastic device and the tcp client will connect to home assistant rather directly to the device. Connecting directly to the meshtastic device will interrupt the home assistant connection. Using python cli, use 'meshtastic --host homeassistant:port'
